Cumulative profit at $5 risk per trade

Closed-trade profit, booked when each trade exits. Fixed $5 risk per trade (no compounding). Binance fees, slippage and real funding included.

The short answer

Recommended — with modest expectations. The strategy made money on all 5 coins over 2020–2026 after realistic costs, including on ZEC, NEAR, ADA, GALA (never used for tuning) and in 2023–26 (never used for tuning).

It wins by catching a few large, clean moves — up or down — and loses slowly in sideways markets. It does not adapt to regimes; it survives them because losses are small and capped.

Start all 5 at equal size, GALA smaller. GALA has a strong edge on paper but the shortest history (from Sep 2021), a thin market, and all of its profit comes from short trades. NEAR has the smallest edge per trade.

Expect long losing streaks (7–9 trades per coin, 20 across all 5), only ~39% winners, and roughly $5.9 a month at $1 risk across the 5 coins.

BB Breakout (4h) · SOL / ZEC / NEAR / ADA / GALA · backtest 2020–2026

1 · How the strategy works and how it was tested

The rules (frozen — not changed for this report)

  • Long: a 4h candle closes above the upper Bollinger band (20 candles, 2σ) and above the 200-candle SMA.
  • Short: a close below the lower band and below the SMA.
  • Stop = the middle band at the signal close · Target = 4× the stop distance · Time exit after 48 candles (8 days).
  • One trade at a time per coin; no pyramiding; no discretion.

Realism: what the backtest charges and assumes

ItemAssumption
DataBinance USDT-M perpetual futures, 4h candles. SOL from Sep 2020, ZEC from Feb 2020, NEAR from Oct 2020, ADA from Jan 2020, GALA from Sep 2021 (listing dates), all to 17–20 Oct 2026.
DecisionOnly at a candle’s close, using only candles already closed. The bot never sees the next candle.
Entry fillNext candle’s open + 0.02% slippage + 0.05% taker fee.
Stop / time exitMarket order: 0.02% slippage + 0.05% taker fee. Gaps through the stop fill at the worse open price.
TargetResting limit (0.02% maker fee) — fills only if price trades 0.05% through it.
Same-candle stop & targetCounted as a stop (worse case). Happened 1 time(s) in 1,508 trades.
FundingReal Binance funding paid or received at every 8h event the trade was open through.
SizingFixed $5 risk per trade on a notional $1,000 account per coin. Equity = $1,000 + cumulative profit.

No look-ahead, no repainting — checked

CoinTruncation cutsOrders comparedMismatchesBot vs app engine
SOL10030,6820308 / 308 identical
ZEC10035,2600332 / 332 identical
NEAR10030,1400297 / 297 identical
ADA10027,3570328 / 328 identical
GALA10023,5560243 / 243 identical
The engine was re-run on data cut at 100 random points per coin; every decision before each cut matched the full-history run, so no future candle is ever used. A second, independently written bot matches the app engine trade for trade.
Tuning status. Bollinger / SMA / stop / time-exit settings were chosen on 2019–22 BTC, ETH and SOL and then frozen. 2023→2026 and every coin except SOL (ZEC, NEAR, ADA, GALA) are out-of-sample. The 4R target was chosen after comparing 3R/4R/5R on all years, so it is mildly in-sample. Coin choice is also hindsight: these 5 were picked from roughly 100 coins screened because they did best (BTC, in the earlier version of this report, was dropped for its weaker, less consistent results), so treat the totals as an optimistic estimate.

BB Breakout (4h) · SOL / ZEC / NEAR / ADA / GALA · backtest 2020–2026

4 · What kind of market does it need?

Every month of every coin (366 coin-months with trades), grouped by how the coin behaved that month. Bars show the average result per trade in those months.

Trend efficiency of the month

Efficiency = net move ÷ total distance travelled by daily closes. Choppy months (< 0.15) average −0.03R per trade; clean trends (≥ 0.50) average +1.21R.

Size of the coin’s move in the month

The clearest pattern: months where the coin moved under 5% average −0.15R per trade; 30%+ months average +0.92R.

Direction of the month

Direction matters little — down months (+0.37R) and up months (+0.67R) both pay. Only the flat middle loses (−0.13R). The SMA filter lets the strategy trade both ways.

How often price crossed the 200-candle SMA

Months that stayed on one side of the SMA made +1.15R per trade (94% profitable). Whipsaw months (9+ crosses) average −0.07R.

Volatility vs the coin’s own typical month

Higher volatility helps: high-volatility months average +0.62R per trade vs +0.12R in quiet months.

In one sentence

The strategy needs the coin to travel a long way in one direction within a few weeks — up or down. It is hurt most by months that go nowhere: flat, choppy months crossing the trend line again and again, when breakouts fail, reverse and hit the stop at the middle band.

Important: these conditions are measured after each month is over. They explain when the strategy makes money, but nobody knows in advance which month will be choppy — section 6 tests whether any of it can be detected at entry.

Only 15%–17% of trades reach the target, but they earn ≈ +3.93R each. Time exits average ≈ +0.85R — trades still open after 8 days are usually still moving the right way. Stops cost ≈ −1.03R each.

What explains the gap

  • Same payoff shape on every coin — wins ≈ +2.21R to +2.41R, losses ≈ −0.93R to −0.98R. The difference is how often breakouts follow through: win rates run 38%–40%.
  • Volatility and costs: typical monthly volatility runs from 83% to 110%, and doubling costs removes only 7%–9% of profit on any coin — none is cost-fragile.
  • Long vs short: GALA made essentially all of its profit on one side (long −$1 / short +$435) — a caution, not a feature. The other coins earn on both sides.
  • Diversification is real: monthly results barely move together (pairwise correlation 0.00 to 0.32). Combined, the worst drawdown was −$128 vs −$315 if each coin’s worst had hit at once.
  • Caution: NEAR has the smallest edge per trade; GALA has the shortest history and the thinnest market (about $13M a day on Binance when checked in Oct 2026).

The most consistent signal: the best breakouts start from compression — low recent volatility and narrow bands — and the worst come after volatility has already expanded. Five conditions were tried, so one pass could partly be luck.

What this means

  • No filter beat the plain strategy on total profit. The chop that hurts it is only visible after the fact; trailing proxies remove good trades along with bad ones.
  • Break-even stops hurt because winners typically dip about −0.39R before working; moving the stop early kills them.
  • Keep the rules frozen. Two ideas (skip breakouts after a strong 10-day trend; trade only from low volatility) raise the average trade in both halves but cut total profit — “fewer, better trades” options worth paper-trading alongside, not replacing, the baseline.
  • Not yet tested: letting winners run past 8 days (time exits average +0.85R), a portfolio-level size brake.

  • Scale is linear: at $5 risk multiply every dollar figure by 5 (drawdown plan ≈ $158).
  • A losing streak of 7–9 trades on one coin is normal — it happened SOL 2×, ZEC 1×, NEAR 0×, ADA 1×, GALA 2× in six years.
  • Recoveries can be slow: ZEC’s worst drawdown took 262 days to recover.
  • Many individual months lose money (131 of 372 coin-months); judge it over quarters, not weeks.

Stop-and-review triggers (set from this history, not tuned)

  • Drawdown deeper than 37R across the 5 coins (beyond the 99% case) → stop and re-examine.
  • Rolling 50-trade result below −22R (worse than the worst 50-trade stretch ever seen) → stop.
  • 4R target-hit rate below ~10% over 60+ trades (history: 15%–17%) → the follow-through the edge depends on has gone.
  • Otherwise do not change the rules mid-drawdown — every losing stretch in this report recovered without changes.

8 · My take: is this strategy recommended?

Verdict

Yes, as a small, rules-only strategy — not as an income source. Across 2020–2026 and 1,508 trades it earned +0.33R per trade after realistic Binance costs and funding, made money on all 5 coins, held up in 2023–26 (never used for tuning), and worked on 4 coins (ZEC, NEAR, ADA, GALA) it had never been tuned on.

It is a classic trend-following breakout: it does not predict or adapt to the market — it waits for big, clean moves and keeps losses small in between. That is why it survived the 2021 mania, the 2022 crash and the 2024–26 ranges without a single losing coin-year.

Is the edge holding up? Average result per trade, by year (all 5 coins)

*2026 to mid-October. 2021 was the strongest year (+0.53R per trade) and 2026* the weakest (+0.23R). Before 2023 the average trade was +0.40R vs +0.29R after — some of the early edge has faded.

Recommended setup

  • Coins: all 5 at equal size to start, GALA at half size until it has live results — shortest history, thinnest market, and all its profit comes from shorts.
  • Rules: exactly as tested — Bollinger 20/2σ, SMA200 filter, stop at the middle band, 4R target, 48-candle time exit.
  • Risk: start at $1 per trade. Plan for a ≈$32 drawdown; expect about $5.9 a month on average (many single months will be negative).
  • Execution: place the target as a resting limit order (maker fee) and the stop at entry; never move the stop early.
  • Review: log every trade and compare with this report each month; use the stop triggers on the previous page.

Proven vs still a hypothesis

Supported by the data

  • Profitable on SOL, ZEC, NEAR, ADA, GALA after costs and funding
  • Big clean moves (either direction) pay; flat months lose
  • Edge per trade ranges from +0.26R (NEAR) to +0.36R (GALA)
  • Coins are only weakly correlated — combined drawdown −$128 vs −$315 if each coin’s worst hit together
  • Break-even stops and whipsaw filters make it worse

Needs more testing

  • That the edge continues — the 4R target was picked with hindsight
  • Coin choice: these 5 were picked from ~100 screened because they did best
  • Skipping breakouts after a strong 10-day trend (better per trade, less total)
  • Low-volatility-only trading (better per trade in both halves, but 52% less profit)
  • Letting winners run past 8 days
  • Why GALA works only on the short side
Backtests describe the past. Past results — even carefully tested, out-of-sample ones — do not guarantee future returns. Trade only money you can afford to lose.
